mission: Continue falsification-first investigation of the GitHub Actions schedule-event materialization S3 regime jump using JANUS journals plus live public primary sources.

inputs.all_journals: Use every journal reference in dossier.journal_ingestion.journal_manifest read-only; fetch the raw current bytes and verify against the recorded Git blob before extracting timing fields.

priority_questions: Did schedule-event creation remain degraded after GitHub's 2026-08-27T00:26Z incident resolution?
Are post-recovery failures specific to schedule while workflow_dispatch/push remain healthy?
Do affected cases span public/private repositories, hosted/self-hosted runners, account ages and off-hour cron minutes?
Does evidence favor transient backlog, lost/stale schedule registration, recurring trigger-processing saturation, deployment fallout, or another control-plane mechanism?
What evidence would falsify the platform-side interpretation?
required_outputs: case graph with source independence labels
superseding receipt when GitHub publishes a detailed RCA
do_not_do: Do not modify historical Record Drift journals.
Do not treat several GitHub Community posts as independent platform telemetry without accounting for copied claims.
Do not infer malicious intent from incomplete status scope.
Do not call scheduler latency R6/R9/R10 record drift.
Do not generate abusive request load; use bounded fetches and cached evidence.
current_best_answer: Observable schedule-specific impact extended beyond the public recovery window and is strongly platform-side in class. Exact causal continuity to the Aug26 database/event-processing defect remains unresolved; deliberate understatement has no evidence.
